summary: clampony preinstall fetches payload from Pastebin / anonymous paste host
details: clampony is a typosquat of the popular `clamp` package: index.js contains the same 5-line clamp() math utility and the README references hughsk/clamp, while package.json adds a `preinstall: node setup.js` lifecycle hook unrelated to that utility. setup.js races `https://pastebin.com/raw/z6K1Rg8J` and `https://calcal.ru/p/t5edjvR/raw` via Promise.any, buffers the response, writes it to a randomUUID filename under os.tmpdir(), and passes the resulting filepath to a run() function. The run() body is empty in this version, but the surrounding code is a complete dropper skeleton — anonymous paste-site source, tmp-staging with a random filename, and a run() hook — and the paste contents are author-mutable, so the executed bytes can change at any time without republishing the package. The destinations are not registry or publisher infrastructure and have no connection to the advertised math utility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
